routes.description: Establish that a simple divine agent provides a better cumulative explanation than naturalism of the universe, uniform laws, life-permitting conditions, embodied conscious agents, and the relevant modal structure.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if theism has a sufficiently stronger combination of comparative prior simplicity and evidential likelihood across the disputed phenomena to be more probable than naturalism.

motionBridge.description: Connect the combined prior and likelihood case to the conclusion that theism is more probable than naturalism.

centralBridges.description: Supply an objective account of simplicity under which one essentially unlimited divine agent can receive a favorable comparative prior.
Show that uniform laws and life-permitting cosmic conditions are more expected given divine reasons than given an uncreated physical reality.
Show that embodied conscious agents with morally significant freedom are expected products of divine goodness and resist an equally simple naturalistic explanation.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Justify applying predictive fit, comparative likelihood, and simplicity as rational explanatory criteria beyond ordinary scientific cases.
Defend a modal framework broad enough to compare the actual universe with alternative possible universes and ultimate explanations.

routes.description: Prevent theism from gaining a comparative probability advantage by supplying economical naturalistic accounts and challenging the claimed objectivity, likelihood advantage, and modal basis of the theistic comparison.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if naturalism remains at least as simple and explanatorily adequate as theism, or if the relevant priors, likelihoods, and modal alternatives do not warrant the claimed comparative probability ordering.

motionBridge.description: Connect naturalistic adequacy and underdetermination in the comparison to denial that theism is more probable than naturalism.

centralBridges.description: Provide a simple naturalistic initial reality and laws capable of explaining subsequent cosmic data without adding a divine agent.
Challenge whether the observed universe, especially its particular contents and production of humans, is more expected under theism.
Show that consciousness can be accommodated through identity theory or another natural emergence account without a decisive theistic advantage.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Frame the dispute as a comparison of equally detailed rivals across priors and the likelihood of the total partitioned evidence.
Ground modal claims in what exists and must exist rather than in conceivability, rational belief, or measures of ignorance.

sections.title: Comparative Method, Simplicity, and Priors
sections.rationale: The probability comparison depends on how explanatory fit and simplicity determine comparative priors, whether qualitative Bayesian dominance is available, and whether adding God unifies data or merely adds complexity.

sections.title: Cosmic Origins, Laws, and Fine-Tuning
sections.rationale: The central cosmic clash concerns whether uniform laws and life-permitting conditions favor purposive divine creation or can follow from an economical naturalistic initial state and its dispositions.

sections.title: Divine Reasons, Anthropocentrism, and Embodied Agency
sections.rationale: Theism's likelihood claim relies on divine reasons to create finite embodied agents, while the comparison must address alternative creations, anthropocentric selection, and what embodiment contributes to morally significant interaction.

sections.title: Consciousness and Naturalistic Explanation
sections.rationale: Consciousness affects explanatory scope because the dispute tests whether privileged access defeats mind-brain identity and whether nonphysical minds could nevertheless arise within naturalism.

sections.title: Modality, Necessity, and Ultimate Explanation
sections.rationale: Accounts of possibility and necessity determine the admissible hypothesis space and whether God, laws, or an initial physical state can function as the ultimate unexplained reality.

chunk-001:D79-C001-02.proposition: Evidence favors a hypothesis when the hypothesis makes the evidence reasonably probable, its negation makes that evidence less probable, and the hypothesis itself is simple.

chunk-001:D79-C001-03.proposition: A perfectly powerful and good God has reason to create embodied conscious agents who can make morally significant free choices between good and evil.

chunk-001:D79-C001-04.proposition: Absent divine creation, the universe's uniform simple laws and their capacity to produce human bodies would be extraordinary coincidences among possible law systems.

chunk-001:D79-C001-05.proposition: The God hypothesis is simple because it postulates one being whose essential omnipotence consists in having no limit on power rather than an arbitrary finite limit.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-02.proposition: A physical initial state capable of producing laws, bodies, and conscious agents would require highly specific causal powers, whereas divine goodness supplies a reason for life-producing powers.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-08.proposition: Mental properties are not identical with publicly accessible physical properties because subjects have privileged and noncontingent access to their own thoughts, feelings, and experiences.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-10.proposition: Theism predicts embodied, conscious, finitely free moral agents in general rather than every human detail, since bodies localize agents and enable morally significant effects on one another.

chunk-003:c003-05.proposition: Metaphysical possibility is ultimately analyzable through logical possibility and the intelligible conceivability of alternative universes.

chunk-003:c003-07.proposition: God is not logically or essence-based necessary, but whichever unexplained ultimate cause exists is ontologically necessary as the final brute fact on which everything else depends.

chunk-001:D79-C001-09.proposition: Theism should be assessed through Bayesian odds against an equally detailed naturalistic rival, comparing their priors and likelihoods on the total evidence rather than considering theism in isolation.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-01.proposition: A single naturalistic initial singularity characterized by few quantities and an inherent disposition to evolve could explain later particles and complexity without adding God, and may therefore be simpler than theism.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-03.proposition: On an actualist account that does not multiply possibilities beyond those required by actual indeterminism, the initial state and laws are necessary, explaining why those cosmic foundations obtain as they do.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-05.proposition: It is gratuitously anthropocentric to treat the universe as arranged for human beings, since its vast numbers of beetles and stars permit equally available descriptions of what it was arranged to produce.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-07.proposition: Mind-brain identity theory offers an economical naturalistic account of consciousness by identifying organisms' mental states and processes with their physical states and processes.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-09.proposition: Even if physicalism about mind is false, naturalism can allow minds to arise from physically complex organisms through a metaphysically natural process without adding enough complexity to make theism inevitably preferable.

chunk-003:c003-03.proposition: A Bayesian comparison can proceed without numerical probabilities when one rival has the higher prior and supplies the better likelihood for every partition of the evidence.

chunk-003:c003-06.proposition: Metaphysical modality concerns what exists and should not be derived from what a reasonable person can believe, because epistemic ignorance has no metaphysical consequences.

chunk-003:c003-08.proposition: Swinburne's ontological necessity closely resembles Oppy's metaphysical necessity and is likewise distinguished from logical necessity, so their modal positions may differ less substantively than their terminology suggests.
